slides.title: Loan Processing Agent
slides.subtitle: Multi-Agent Orchestration with Google ADK on OpenShift AI

slides.title: End-to-end loan processing — fully automated, fully auditable

stats.label: One orchestrator coordinates four specialist sub-agents via ADK AgentTool
9-doc regulatory corpus (SBA, ECOA, Reg B) retrieved at underwriting and decision time
Human-in-the-loop pause after pricing — no loan approved without explicit user consent
SQLite-backed state persistence enables repair & resume across pod restarts and sessions

slides.title: Why multiple agents instead of one big prompt?

items.label: Focused Prompts
items.description: Each agent has one job, its own system prompt, and a Pydantic output schema. No cross-stage contamination

items.label: Isolated Tools
items.description: Sub-agents only get the tools they need. PricingAgent can't call finalize_loan_decision. No tool leakage

items.label: Testable Boundaries
items.description: Each agent writes structured output to a session state key. Test underwriting in isolation, swap pricing logic independently

items.label: Locked Down
items.description: Sub-agents set disallow_transfer_to_parent and disallow_transfer_to_peers to True. They can't call other agents

slides.title: AutoRAG — retrieval-augmented regulatory knowledge
leftItems: OGX vector store — Milvus + nomic-embed-text-v1.5 embeddings
UnderwritingAgent: 1 LLM tool call → internally 2 AutoRAG queries (eligibility rules + industry guidance)
LoanDecisionAgent: internal auto-call on decline path (ECOA adverse action via retrieve_regulatory_guidance)
max_num_results=3 per query — focused, low-latency retrieval
Graceful degradation: falls back to static eligibility_rules.json if AutoRAG unavailable
rightItems: Adverse action notice rules (ECOA / Reg B)

slides.title: Callbacks — guardrails at every lifecycle point
rows: Parses loan ID (SBL-YYYY-XXXXX) from user message; stores inline documents for later injection
Blocks execution if process is halted, completed, or pricing should be skipped (INELIGIBLE)
Injects PDF/image into LLM request context — DocumentExtractionAgent only
Persists sub-agent output to SQLite; detects INELIGIBLE → flags PricingAgent skip
Second LLM call validates trajectory, grounding, completeness. Fail → response blocked
slides.note: LLM-as-Judge: checks tool order, verifies all numbers match structured outputs, confirms nothing missing. Fails closed — blocked response, not hallucinated data.

slides.title: Repair and resume — surviving failures and restarts
leftItems: Layer 1: ADK session state — in-memory, fast, lost on pod restart
Layer 2: SQLite via ProcessStateService — persistent on PVC, full model_dump() of every agent output
Layer 3: check_process_status — always first tool call, bridges SQLite → ADK session on resume
Layer 4: _load_step_data_from_db() — last-resort fallback inside finalize_loan_decision for cross-turn sessions
rightItems: Pod restart between pricing and approval → SQLite reloads completed steps into fresh session
Missing data mid-pipeline → agent halts, asks user, resumes from exact step
User returns hours later in new session → check_process_status picks up where it left off
Approval in fresh API session → _load_step_data_from_db() loads all prior outputs from SQLite

slides.title: What this looks like on OpenShift AI

items.label: Model Serving (MaaS)
items.description: Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenAI-compatible endpoint through LiteLLM. Switch to Vertex AI or direct API key by changing env vars

items.label: AutoRAG (OGX)
items.description: 9-doc regulatory corpus in Milvus + nomic-embed-text-v1.5. Queried 3× per loan: 2 at underwriting, 1 at loan decision

items.label: MLflow Tracing
items.description: Optional — set MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI and every LiteLLM call auto-logs as spans. Degrades gracefully if unavailable

items.label: OpenShift AI Deployment
items.description: FastAPI container, PVC for SQLite, ConfigMap for tunable params, SealedSecrets for API key, OpenShell network isolation

slides.title: Skills — domain knowledge loaded on demand
rows: Step-by-step HITL workflow: extract → underwrite → price → approve/decline
5 SBA eligibility rules, risk flags, status definitions
Risk tier table (Tier 1–4), rate ranges, presentation format, approval prompt
ECOA requirements, decline letter template, tone and compliance guidance
slides.note: Only the orchestrator has SkillToolset. Sub-agents are locked: disallow_transfer_to_parent=True, disallow_transfer_to_peers=True.

slides.title: What a real conversation looks like
bullets: **User:** "Process loan SBL-2026-10001: Acme Bakery, $150K, 5 years, $420K revenue..."
**Pipeline:** check_process_status → load_skill → DocumentExtractionAgent → UnderwritingAgent + 2 RAG queries → PricingAgent
**Agent:** "Acme Bakery qualifies as Tier 2 (Moderate Risk). 7.75% rate, $3,012.43/mo, 60 months. **Do you approve?**"
**Pipeline:** check_process_status (reload from SQLite) → LoanDecisionAgent → LLM-as-Judge → response
**Agent:** "Loan SBL-2026-10001 approved. Approval letter generated (ref: DL-2026-10001)."
